pull.title: test: use long timeout for event waits in interface_ipc_mining
pull.body:
Follow-up to #36791, https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36791#discussion_r4565761925 by ryanofsky.

#36791 fixed the `waitTipChanged` timeout on slow hosts, but the `template6` `waitNext` call has the same race: it waits for an event the test triggers after a 0.1s sleep, with a 1s timeout.

This adds `long_ipc_timeout` and uses it for all waits that end on an event the test triggers.

To reproduce failure on master:

```diff
diff --git a/test/functional/interface_ipc_mining.py b/test/functional/interface_ipc_mining.py
index cdef196fd0..49e1c8a9c1 100755
--- a/test/functional/interface_ipc_mining.py
+++ b/test/functional/interface_ipc_mining.py
@@ -320,7 +320,8 @@ class IPCMiningTest(BitcoinTestFramework):
                 self.log.debug("Wait for another, get one after increase in fees in the mempool")
                 template6 = await wait_and_do(
                     mining_wait_next_template(template5, stack, ctx, waitoptions),
-                    lambda: self.miniwallet.send_self_transfer(fee_rate=10, from_node=self.nodes[0]))
+                    lambda: self.miniwallet.send_self_transfer(fee_rate=10, from_node=self.nodes[0]),
+                    sleep_time=1.2)
                 assert template6 is not None
                 block4 = await mining_get_block(template6, ctx)
                 assert_equal(len(block4.vtx), 3)

```

test: use long timeout for event waits in interface_ipc_mining

hosts with the 1s default. Use a long timeout for all of them.

Tested ACK 74135e2e625030b18daf7539bd19dabb75948af1. This finishes the fix from #36791: every wait that returns on an event the test triggers now has at least a minute, so none of them can time out on a slow host with the default timeout factor. I checked that the test passes normally, with the faketime command from #36791, and with `sleep_time=1.2` on the `template6` wait, which failed before.

The waits still using `default_ipc_timeout` (`template4`, `template5` and the two `waitNext` policy tests) are fine as they are: the fees they wait for are already in the mempool, and `waitNext` always checks fees once after its first one-second tick, however short the timeout.
this uncovers a pre-existing bug for large timeout factor values

comments.diff_hunk:
@@ -879,6 +879,9 @@ def run_test(self):
         self.miniwallet = MiniWallet(self.nodes[0])
         # Amount of time in milliseconds the test is allowed to wait or be idle before it should fail.
         self.default_ipc_timeout = 1000.0 * self.options.timeout_factor
+        # Timeout for waits that should return early because of an event the test
+        # triggers, long enough not to expire on a slow host.
+        self.long_ipc_timeout = max(self.default_ipc_timeout, 60000.0)  # at least 1 minute
comments.body: nit: Just like below (`no_event_timeout_ms`), it would be good to include the type here. Everything in the python tests is usually denoted in float seconds, so it would be good to mark the places that are not.

(recall the sleep time here is seconds, not ms)

This is a pre-existing bug, but the changes in this pull will now cause the tests to deterministically fail with a high timeout factor, because the `long_ipc_timeout` (`~1s*factor`) would happen before the generate after `1.1s *factor`.

As a regression test against `feeThreshold = MAX_MONEY`, the sleep only needs to ensure that the one-second fee-check tick elapses. Scaling it makes the test unnecessarily slow, adding roughly timeout_factor seconds of idle time to every run.

The correct sleep to use here is 1.1s, or maybe 2s, if you want to allow for more machines to hit the tick, but if a machine is slower than that to call a simple IPC call, it doesn't seem worth it to accommodate in the test (and slow down all of our CI runs).

Fixed in https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36924


Also, I am a bit confused about the 60s floor of long_ipc_timeout. Why is it needed? `default_ipc_timeout` is already scaled by the timeout factor to accommodate slow machines, so it seems confusing to have a different variable to track the same thing? I'd say `long_ipc_timeout` should be removed.

Quoting from https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36791#discussion_r4565751670:

>Use a 1 minute timeout for the waitTipChanged call that waits for a newly mined block, instead of default_ipc_timeout, which is only 1 second when the test runs with the default --timeout-factor (CI uses 40).

>The test sends waitTipChanged, waits 0.1 seconds, and then calls generate. Everything between the node receiving the request and the new block becoming its tip (the rest of that sleep, the generate RPC, and creating, validating and connecting the block) had to fit in that 1 second, which a busy machine may not manage. When it didn't, waitTipChanged returned the old tip and the height check failed. The longer timeout costs nothing when the test passes, because the call returns as soon as the tip changes.

The reasoning is that this could fail in slow machines (laptop) that run with default timeout factor, though idk if this was seen on real hardware before.

Ah thx for the reference. The general idea is that the tests should pass on any idk mid-range machine (even laptop) sold in the last few years with the default timeout-factor.

* So if the `default_ipc_timeout` is too small to accommodate that, it should just be increased maybe from 1s to 2s. (Such a change should be harmless, because in the happy path it should still pass as fast as your machine is)
* However, if someone is running an ancient/slow machine, or heavy virtualization or heavy sanitizers, there is just no other fix than to increase the timeout-factor on their command line. Fixing the tests for that seems odd.

So I haven't tried it, but I think in your command:

```
faketime --exclude-monotonic -f "+0 x0.1" build/test/functional/interface_ipc_mining.py
```

you can increase the --timeout-factor, because a 10x relative speed doesn't seem like normal hardware.

I think there is one more place which can spell out the fee tick wait explicitly:

```diff
diff --git a/test/functional/interface_ipc_mining.py b/test/functional/interface_ipc_mining.py
index 55b90f5..cec9c78 100755
--- a/test/functional/interface_ipc_mining.py
+++ b/test/functional/interface_ipc_mining.py
@@ -320,3 +320,4 @@ class IPCMiningTest(BitcoinTestFramework):
                 self.log.debug("Wait for another, get one after increase in fees in the mempool")
-                waitoptions.timeout = self.long_ipc_timeout
+                # Allow the normal event wait as well as one fee check tick.
+                waitoptions.timeout = self.default_ipc_timeout_ms + 1000
                 template6 = await wait_and_do(
```

Everything else can use the `default_ipc_timeout_ms` and `long_ipc_timeout` can be removed.
